surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the removal of N double bonds in the precursor molecule, which is more difficult than the removal of single bonded N ligands. The removal of these N double bonds is critical for the formation of MoC_x and is facilitated by a hydrogen radical rich plasma. The carbon content in the MoC_xNy film is believed to originate from the (tBuN)2(NMe2)2Mo precursor and becomes available for cross bridging during the H2 rich plasma process step. Chiu et al. proposed an m-methyl activation of the tertbutyl groups forming MeCN and HCN, followed by Mo-N bond disassociation as the mechanism for molybdenum carbonitride formation with a CVD process at temperatures >300 /C14 C with Mo(NBut)2(NHBut)2.
